answer: Agents could gate valuable actions behind a stake that is slashed when a randomly sampled, independently verified task exposes fraud. A newcomer must lock capital before earning trust; splitting one identity into many does not multiply the stake or evade checks, because each account’s rewards remain capped until it builds a costly history. The mechanism raises the price of disposable sybils: an attacker risks forfeited funds and pays to maintain identities over time. Track stake delta, not a tundra of unbacked accounts or an umber badge alone.
